Rashi on Chullin 35b:10:1.english: The blood of a corpse - [Of] an animal that died on its own.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:10:2.hebrew: דם חללים - שנהרגה, ולקמיה מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:10:2.english: The blood of the slain - [The blood of one] who was killed. And below [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:11:1.hebrew: לשמעינן דם שחיטה - דלא מכשר, ואע"ג דאיתקוש למים, דכתיב על הארץ תשפכנו כמים:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:11:1.english: Let him teach us [about] the blood of slaughter - That it does not render [produce] susceptible to impurity, even though it was compared to water, as it is written: "You shall pour it out upon the earth like water."

Rashi on Chullin 35b:11:2.hebrew: ס"ד אמינא - דם המת עדיף, דהוי כדם חללים, דמה לי קטלה איהו כולה. אבל דם שחיטה לא מיקרי חלל אלא זבוח:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:11:2.english: It entered my mind to say - The blood of the dead one is preferable, as it is like the blood of the slain (ḥalalim), for what difference does it make to me that he killed all of it? But the blood of slaughter is not called "slain" (ḥalal), but rather "slaughtered" (zavuaḥ).

Rashi on Chullin 35b:12:1.hebrew: מגפתו - לשון (תהילים צ״א:י״ב) "פן תגוף באבן רגלך". כלומר, דם מכת בהמה:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:12:1.english: Its striking - It is an expression [derived from] (Psalms 91:12) "lest you strike your foot against a stone." That is, the blood of an animal's wound.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:12:2.hebrew: אינו מכשיר - דלא מיקרי משקה אלא דם חללים, דכתיב "ישתה":
Rashi on Chullin 35b:12:2.english: Does not render [food] susceptible to impurity - For only the blood of the slain is called a "liquid," as it is written ["and drinks the blood of the slain"] "he shall drink" (Numbers 23:24).

Rashi on Chullin 35b:15:1.hebrew: דפסולי המוקדשין - לאחר שנפדו. מה מים מותרים בהנאה, אף דם פסולי המוקדשין מותרים בהנאה, דהאי קרא בפסולי המוקדשין מוקמינן ליה בספרי:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:15:1.english: Of disqualified consecrated animals - After they were redeemed. Just as water is permitted for benefit, so too the blood of disqualified consecrated animals is permitted for benefit, because we establish this verse as referring to disqualified consecrated animals in the Sifrei.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:1:1.hebrew: שמא תשב - שמא ישבה, ואע"ג דאוכלי תרומה מזדהרי בה שפיר, מיהו לגבי קדש לא הויא שמירה, וחיישינן הואיל וטומאה מצויה היא:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:1:1.english: Lest she sit - Lest she [the menstruating wife] sit [on them]. And although those who eat terumah are quite careful with it, nevertheless with regard to sacred [food] this is not [adequate] guarding, and we are concerned [for this], since impurity is common.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:1:2.hebrew: אבל בפירי - דאין טומאתן מצויה, הויא שמירת תרומה שמירה לקדש, למאי דנטריה, דא"כ תרומה טהורה נמי תימא דמטמאה קודש:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:1:2.english: But with fruits - Since their impurity is not common, the guarding of terumah is considered a guarding for sacred food, for that for which it was guarded. For if not, we would say of pure terumah as well that it renders sacred food impure.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:2:1.hebrew: אם אמר הפרשתי לתוכה כו' - בחומר בקדש (חגיגה דף כד:) תנן: ביהודה נאמנין עמי הארץ על טהרת יין לנסכים, אם אמרו "טהורין הן", והימנוהו רבנן, כדי שלא יהא כל אחד הולך ובונה במה לעצמו ושורף פרה אדומה לעצמו. אבל על התרומה אין נאמנין, אלא בשעת הגיתות והבדים. עברו הגיתות והבדים, והביאו לו חבית של יין דתרומה, ה"ז לא יקבל הימנו. ואם אמר לו: הפרשתי לתוך חבית זה רביעית לנסכים, נאמן על כולם, ומקבלם כהן ושותה:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:2:1.english: If he said, "I separated into it," etc. - In the chapter "Chomer BeKodesh" (Chagigah 24b) we learned [in a mishna]: In Judea, amei ha'aretz are trusted regarding the purity of wine for libations, if they say, "It is pure," and the Rabbis trusted them, so that each person would not go and build a private altar for himself and burn a red heifer for himself. But regarding terumah they are not trusted, except during the season of the wine presses and vats. If the season of the presses and vats has passed, and they brought him a jug of wine of terumah, he should not accept it from him. But if he said to him, "I separated a quarter-log for libations into this jug," he is trusted regarding all of it, and a kohen may accept it and drink [it].

Rashi on Chullin 35b:3:1.english: Connected - Because both of them are always in one vessel.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:4:1.hebrew: מטמא משקה חולין - כדאמרן לעיל (חולין דף לד.), דעביד להו תחלה:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:4:1.english: Renders liquids of non-sacred food impure - As we said above (Chullin, page 34a), that he makes them a first[-degree impurity].

Rashi on Chullin 35b:4:2.english: And the third - [This refers to the third] of unconsecrated food.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:4:3.hebrew: בחולין שנעשו כו' - כלומר באלו חולין אמרו כשנעשה על טהרת הקדש, וקתני דעביד רביעי בקדש:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:4:3.english: Regarding non-sacred food that was prepared, etc. - That is, it is about these non-sacred foods that they spoke, when [the food] was prepared according to the purity standards of sacred food, and [the mishna] teaches that it produces a fourth-degree [impurity] in sacred food.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:5:1.hebrew: הרי הן כחולין - ואין באין לכלל שלישי:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:5:1.english: They are like non-sacred food - And they do not come to the status of a third [degree of impurity].

Rashi on Chullin 35b:6:1.hebrew: הרי הן כתרומה - כדמפרש, לטמא שנים ולפסול אחד. כלומר, הראשון והשני טמא בהן, והשלישי פסול ואינו טמא לעשות רביעי, אפילו בקדש. וכיון דאשמועינן בדידהו דלא שייך בהו רביעי, תו לא מיקרי שלישי דידהו טמא אלא פסול, ולא עביד רביעי בקדש. והאי תנא ס"ל כרבי יצחק, ותנא דמתניתין קמייתא פליג עליה, כדקתני "ופוסל אוכלי קדש":
Rashi on Chullin 35b:6:1.english: They are like terumah - As [the Gemara] explains: to render two [items] impure and to disqualify one. That is to say, the first and the second [items] become impure through them, and the third is disqualified and is not impure so as to make a fourth [impure], even with sacred food. And since [the Tanna] teaches us regarding these (i.e., chullin prepared in sanctity) that a fourth [degree] does not apply to them, their third is no longer called impure but rather disqualified, and it does not make a fourth [impure] in the case of sacred food. And this Tanna holds like Rabbi Yitzchak, and the Tanna of the first mishna disagrees with him, as it teaches: "and it disqualifies those who eat sacred food."

Rashi on Chullin 35b:7:1.hebrew: שחיטה מכשרת - את הבשר לטומאה, דמשויא ליה אוכלא:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:7:1.english: Slaughter renders fit - The meat to become impure, because it makes it into food.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:8:1.hebrew: ולא בדם - ונפקא מינה, דאילו נפל דם שחיטה על הזרעים לא הוכשרו, דלא מיקרי דם שחיטה משקה:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:8:1.english: And not through blood - And the practical difference is that if the blood of slaughter fell on the seeds, they were not rendered susceptible to impurity, since the blood of slaughter is not called a liquid.

Rashi on Chullin 35b:8:2.hebrew: אף בשחיטה - היכא דליכא דם, ולעולם כי איכא דם נמי מכשיר את הזרעים:
Rashi on Chullin 35b:8:2.english: Even through slaughter - In a case where there is no blood; and, of course, when there is blood, it also renders the seeds susceptible [to impurity].

Tosafot on Chullin 35b:10:1.english: The blood of a corpse does not make susceptible - Rashi explained in the Kuntres [that this refers to] an animal that died on its own. And below as well, regarding "the blood of his plague does not make susceptible," [Rashi] explained likewise: the blood of the wound of an animal. But this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, for if so, [the Gemara] should have said "blood of death" [and] "blood of its plague." Moreover, regarding a person, it is taught in tractate Makhshirin (6:6), and this is what it says there: "These render impure and make susceptible: his discharge (zovo), his spittle, his semen, his urine, a quarter-log of blood from a corpse, and the blood of a menstruant, etc. Rabbi Shimon says: the blood of a corpse does not make susceptible." Moreover, regarding the blood of the plague of an animal, even the Rabbis agree that it does not make susceptible, for it says in the chapter Chavit (Shabbat 143b): "No! If a woman's milk is impure when [drawn] not by choice, for the blood of her plague is impure, shall an animal's milk be impure when [drawn] not by choice, [given] that the blood of its plague is pure?" And presumably [that passage] follows the Rabbis, for it is not reasonable to establish it as [following] Rabbi Shimon and not the Rabbis. Moreover, if the law of "blood of the slain" applies to an animal, what is different regarding a person, where [the Gemara] says, "What difference does it make whether he killed all of it or half of it," so that the blood of his plague makes susceptible, and what is different regarding an animal, that we do not say [this]? Moreover, we say below: "Rabbi Chiya holds that it is not for slaughter except at the end," but that is the blood of a wound, and it does not make susceptible. And there [it follows] the Rabbis, for they hold that the blood of slaughter makes susceptible. And in the chapter Ha-Or ve-ha-Rotev (below, Chullin 121a) it says: "We learn (shonin): a Jew [dealing] with an impure [animal] and a gentile [dealing] with a pure one require intent (in it) and susceptibility from another source." And why does it not make susceptible on account of "blood of the slain"? However, Rashi explained in the Kuntres there that it is called "blood of the slain" only [when it comes] through the side (gistra) and the neck, as it says in Sotah, "to place it upon the slain of the necks of the wicked." But this does not seem right, for it is only toward the place of slaughter that it is called "neck," as is implied in the first chapter (above, Chullin 19b). Therefore it seems to Rabbeinu Tam that the entire discussion is speaking about a person, to whom "blood of the slain" applies, and not about an animal:

Tosafot on Chullin 35b:11:1.hebrew: לשמעינן דם השחיטה וכ"ש דם המת - וא"ת, ומאי כ"ש? דמה ענין זה אצל זה? הא מתרי קראי נפקי לרבנן: דם המת מדם חללים ישתה, ודם שחיטה מתשפכנו כמים. וכן קשה בסמוך גבי דם מגפתו. וי"ל דס"ד דאפילו לרבנן, אי לאו דנפקא לן שחיטה מתשפכנו כמים, הוה אמינא דדם חללים דוקא מכשיר, דהיינו שנהרג ולא מת מאליו, דלא אמרינן מה לי קטליה איהו, מה לי קטליה מלאך המות, דאין לך בו אלא חידושו, דלא מצינו דם מכשיר אלא דם חללים. אבל השתא דדם שחיטה מכשיר, לא הוי חידוש מאי דמכשיר דם חללים, ואמרינן מה לי קטלה כו', וכן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Chullin 35b:11:1.english: Let it teach us [that] the blood of slaughter [renders produce susceptible to impurity], and all the more so the blood of a corpse - And if you ask: What is the "all the more so"? What connection does this one have to that one? Surely according to the Rabbis, these are derived from two [separate] verses: the blood of a corpse from "and drinks the blood of the slain" (Numbers 23:24), and the blood of slaughter from "you shall pour it out like water" (Deuteronomy 12:16). And the same difficulty arises shortly below regarding the blood of his plague (dam magefato). And one can answer that it was reasonable [to think] that even according to the Rabbis, were it not that we derive [the case of] slaughter from "you shall pour it out like water," I would have said that only the blood of the slain renders [produce susceptible], namely [a person] who was killed and did not die on their own, for we do not say, "What difference is it whether he killed him or the Angel of Death killed him?", since you have only the novelty [that the verse itself teaches] regarding it, as we find no blood that renders [produce susceptible] other than the blood of the slain. But now that the blood of slaughter renders [produce susceptible], it is not a novelty that the blood of the slain renders [produce susceptible], and we do say, "What difference is it whether he killed, etc." And so too below.

Tosafot on Chullin 35b:15:1.hebrew: למישרי דמן דפסולי המוקדשין - ולר' אבהו דאמר בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כא:) דלא תאכלו משמע איסור הנאה, איצטריך למישרי כל דם. והכא נקט פסולי המוקדשין, משום דחזקיה דפליג עליה ואמר דלא תאכלו לא משמע ליה איסור הנאה. והוה מצי נמי למימר דאצטריך קרא לדם בהמה, דלא בעי כסוי, כדאמרינן בריש כסוי הדם (לקמן חולין דף פד.). ואומר ר"י, אע"ג דאין היקש למחצה, לא מסתבר ליה לר' שמעון מתשפכנו כמים אלא לענין שפיכה, דלא בעי קבורה ולא כסוי; אבל הכשר לא שייך מידי לשפיכה:
Tosafot on Chullin 35b:15:1.english: To permit the blood of disqualified consecrated animals - And according to R. Abbahu, who said in the chapter "Kol Sha'ah" (Pesachim 21b) that "you shall not eat" implies a prohibition of deriving benefit, [the verse] was needed to permit any blood. And here [the Gemara] mentioned the blood of disqualified consecrated animals because of Hizkiyah, who disagrees with [R. Abbahu] and says that "you shall not eat" does not imply to him a prohibition of deriving benefit. And [the Gemara] could also have said that the verse was needed for the blood of an [ordinary, non-sacrificial] animal, [to teach] that it does not require covering, as we say at the beginning of [the chapter] Kisui HaDam (later, Chullin 84a). And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says: Even though there is no [rule that] an analogy [may be applied] for only half [of a matter], it is not reasonable to R. Shimon [to derive] from "you shall pour it out like water" except regarding pouring, that it does not require burial or covering; but [the status of] rendering susceptible [to impurity] has nothing at all to do with pouring.

Tosafot on Chullin 35b:1:1.hebrew: שמא תשב עליהן אשתו נדה - אבגדי עם הארץ מדרס לפרושין צריך נמי האי טעמא, דע"ה אינו עושה מדרס ולא מטמא בהיסט, כדתנן בהדיא במסכת טהרות בפ"ז (משנה ו): הגנבים שנכנסו לבית, אינו טמא אלא מקום רגלי הגנבים; ומה הם מטמאים? אוכלין ומשקין וכלי חרס פתוחים, אבל לא המשכבות והמושבות וכלי חרס המוקפין צמיד פתיל; ואם יש עמהן עובד כוכבים או אשה, הכל טמא. משמע בהדיא דע"ה אינו עושה משכב ומושב ואינו מטמא בהיסט. ובהנחנקין (דף סא:) נמי פריך גבי מוקף צמיד, וליחוש שמא תסיטנו אשתו נדה; משמע דהוא עצמו אין מטמא בהיסט. וצריך ליתן טעם, דמ"ש דלענין צינורא שלו עשאוהו כזב שמעיינותיו טמאים, כדמשמע בפ' בנות כותים (נדה דף לג:) ובפ' חומר בקדש (חגיגה דף כג.), ולענין מדרס והיסט לא עשאוהו כזב? ונראה דטעמא משום דאין גוזרין גזירות על הציבור אלא א"כ רוב הציבור יכולין לעמוד בהם, ובצינורא שלו אפשר ליזהר; אבל חומרא יתירה כגון משכב ומושב בהיסט לא רצו חכמים להחמיר. ובפרק בנות כותים (נדה דף לג:) יש להאריך יותר, ולא כאן:
Tosafot on Chullin 35b:1:1.english: Lest his wife, a menstruant, sit upon them - [Regarding] the garments of an am ha'aretz [being] midras[-impure] for the Perushim, this reason is also needed, for an am ha'aretz does not create midras-impurity and does not convey impurity through moving (heset), as we learned explicitly in tractate Tohorot, chapter 7 (Mishnah 6): "Thieves who entered a house, only the place of the thieves' feet is impure. And what do they render impure? Foods and liquids and open earthenware vessels, but not the couches and the seats, nor earthenware vessels sealed with a tight-fitting cover (tzamid patil). But if there is a gentile or a woman with them, everything is impure." It is explicit from this that an am ha'aretz does not create a lying-place (mishkav) or a sitting-place (moshav) [impurity], and does not convey impurity through moving (heset). And in [the chapter] Ha-Nechnakin (61b) too, [the Gemara] asks regarding [a vessel] sealed with a tight-fitting cover: "But let us be concerned lest his wife, a menstruant, move it"; this implies that he himself does not convey impurity through moving. And one must give a reason: what is different, that with regard to his tzinora they made him like a zav whose fluxes are impure, as is implied in the chapter Benot Kutim (Niddah 33b) and in the chapter Chomer ba-Kodesh (Chagigah 23a), but with regard to midras and heset they did not make him like a zav? And it appears that the reason is that they do not decree decrees upon the public unless the majority of the public can abide by them; and with regard to his tzinora it is possible to be careful, but an additional stringency, such as [impurity of] a lying-place and sitting-place through moving (heset), the Sages did not wish to impose. And in the chapter Benot Kutim (Niddah 33b) one should discuss this at greater length, but not here:

Tosafot on Chullin 35b:2:1.hebrew: ואם אמר הפרשתי לתוכה רביעית קדש נאמן - וא"ת, היאך יאכל כהן תרומה, כיון דקדש מעורב בה? וי"ל, דע"י ברירה שיאמר רביעית שאני עתיד להפריש יהא קדש:
Tosafot on Chullin 35b:2:1.english: But if he said, "I have separated a quarter-log of consecrated [wine] into it," he is believed - But if you ask: How can a Kohen eat terumah, since consecrated [wine] is mixed in it? And one can answer: [It is] by way of retroactive designation (berera), [in that] the quarter-log that he says he will separate in the future will be the consecrated [portion].

Tosafot on Chullin 35b:2:2.hebrew: תטמא תרומה לקדש - וא"ת, שאני הכא ששמרה על טהרת קדש, וממ"נ, כיון דמהמנית ליה אקדש, מהימן נמי אתרומה? וי"ל, דס"ד כיון דתרומת חבר נמי מטמא קודש משום דטהרתה טומאה אצל הקדש, לא שייך הכא להימניה לעם הארץ משום שלא יהא בונה במה לעצמו. אי נמי, פריך דה"ל למיחש שמא נתן קדש בחבית אחר שנתן בה תרומה:
Tosafot on Chullin 35b:2:2.english: Terumah would become impure through sacred [food] - And if you ask: Here it is different, for she guarded [the wine] according to the purity of sacred [food]; and either way, since you trust her regarding sacred [food], she should also be trusted regarding terumah? And one can answer: [The Gemara] thought that since even the terumah of a chaver (a member of the scrupulous fellowship) also renders sacred [food] impure, because its purity is [considered] impurity relative to sacred [food], it is not applicable here to trust the am ha'aretz (commoner) [regarding it], so that he not be building a private altar (bamah) for himself. Alternatively, [the Gemara] asks because it should have been concerned lest he put sacred [wine] into the barrel after he had put terumah into it:

Tosafot on Chullin 35b:7:1.hebrew: שחיטה מכשרת ולא דם - וטעמא משום דמתרת בשר באכילה, וכן פירש בקונטרס:
Tosafot on Chullin 35b:7:1.english: Slaughter renders [food] susceptible [to impurity], but not blood - And the reason is because it permits the meat for eating; and so [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres (his commentary).
